contents.html: The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in Federal information systems.
contents.html_ja: 米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の情報技術研究所（ITL）は、国の計測・標準インフラストラクチャに対する技術的なリーダーシップを提供することにより、米国の経済と公共の福祉を促進しています。ITL は、情報技術の発展と生産的な利用を推進するため、テスト、テスト方法、参照データ、概念実証の実装、技術的分析を開発しています。ITL の責務には、連邦情報システムにおける国家安全保障に関係しない情報について、費用対効果の高いセキュリティとプライバシーを実現するための、マネジメント、管理、技術、物理面の標準およびガイドラインの策定が含まれます。

contents.html: This publication has been developed by NIST to further its statutory responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA), Public Law (P.L.) 107-347. NIST is responsible for developing information security standards and guidelines, including minimum requirements for Federal information systems, but such standards and guidelines shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate Federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems. contents.html: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are hybrid networked cyber and engineered physical elements co-designed to create adaptive and predictive systems for enhanced performance.<sup>1, 2</sup> These smart systems present a key opportunity to create a competitive advantage for U.S. industrial innovation and to improve the performance and reliability of new and existing systems. From smart manufacturing and the electric smart grid, to smart structures and transportation systems, CPS will pervasively impact the economy and society.
contents.html_ja: サイバーフィジカルシステム（Cyber-Physical Systems、CPS）は、ネットワーク接続されたサイバー要素と工学的に設計された物理要素が融合し、性能を高めるための適応型で予測的なシステムを作り出すように共同設計されたものです。<sup>1, 2</sup> これらのスマートシステムは、米国の産業イノベーションにおける競争優位を生み出し、新規および既存のシステムの性能と信頼性を向上させる重要な機会をもたらします。スマート製造や電力スマートグリッドから、スマート構造物や交通システムに至るまで、CPS は経済と社会に広く影響を与えるでしょう。

contents.html_ja: サイバーセキュリティは、サイバーフィジカルシステム、その情報、およびそれを支える通信と情報インフラストラクチャが、適切に保護されているという確信を与える、重要な分野横断的な領域です。CPS は、重要インフラストラクチャなどの環境で、ますます利用されるようになっています。しかし、CPS には、リアルタイムの応答や、きわめて高い可用性、予測可能性、信頼性が必要であるなど、多くの固有の特性があり、これがサイバーセキュリティに関する判断に影響を与えます。
contents.html: Cybersecurity is a critical cross-cutting discipline that provides confidence that cyber-physical systems, their information, and supporting communications and information infrastructures are adequately safeguarded. CPS are increasingly being utilized in critical infrastructures and other settings. However, CPS have many unique characteristics, including the need for real-time response and extremely high availability, predictability, and reliability, which impacts cyber-security decisions.

contents.html_ja: NIST は現在、電力スマートグリッド、スマート製造、スマートビルディング、ネットワーク接続された自動車など、複数の CPS 分野に取り組んでいます。この取り組みは、工学研究所（Engineering Laboratory、EL）が主導していますが、物理計測研究所（Physical Measurement Laboratory、PML）と情報技術研究所（ITL）も参加しています。ITL には、CPS の進化にとって重要な、相互運用性、ユーザビリティ、信頼性、セキュリティといった、複数の主要な専門分野があります。2009 年以降、NIST はスマートグリッドの分野できわめて活発に活動してきました。ITL は、通信ネットワーク、タイミング、サイバーセキュリティなど、関連する複数の分野でリーダーシップと専門知識を提供し、きわめて活発に活動してきました。ITL のコンピューターセキュリティ部門（CSD）は、Smart Grid Interoperability Panel の Cyber Security Working Group にリーダーシップと専門知識を提供してきました。関連分野における幅広い専門知識を活かして、私たちは現在、サイバーフィジカルシステムのより広い全体像と、その中でサイバーセキュリティがどう位置づけられるかを検討しています。
contents.html: NIST is currently working in several CPS areas, including the electric smart grid, smart manufacturing, smart buildings, and networked automobiles. This work is being led by the Engineering Laboratory (EL), but also includes the Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML) and the Information Technology Laboratory (ITL). ITL has a number of key areas of expertise that are important to the evolution of CPS−interoperability, usability, reliability, and security. Since 2009, NIST has been very active in the area of the smart grid. ITL has been very active, providing leadership and expertise in a number of relevant areas, including communication networks, timing, and cybersecurity. ITL’s Computer Security Division (CSD) has provided leadership and expertise to the Smart Grid Interoperability Panel’s Cyber Security Working Group. Leveraging our broad expertise in relevant areas, we are now looking at the broader landscape of cyber-physical systems, and how cybersecurity fits into that landscape.

contents.html: Dr. Arnold joined the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in September 2006 as Deputy Director, Technology Services, after a 33-year career in the telecommunications and information technology industry. He was appointed National Coordinator for Smart Grid Interoperability at in April 2009. He has been responsible for leading the development of standards underpinning the nation’s Smart Grid. In October 2011, Dr. Arnold added an additional role as Director of Cyber Physical Systems within NIST’s Engineering Laboratory (EL). Anticipating and meeting the measurement science and standards needs for technology-intensive manufacturing construction, and cyber-physical systems in ways that enhance economic prosperity and improve the quality of life , EL promotes U.S. innovation and industrial competitiveness in areas of critical national priority.

contents.html: The goal of the DHS National Cyber Security Division's CSSP is to reduce industrial control system risks within and across all critical infrastructure and key resource sectors by coordinating efforts among federal, state, local, and tribal governments, as well as industrial control systems owners, operators and vendors. The CSSP coordinates activities to reduce the likelihood of success and severity of impact of a cyber attack against critical infrastructure control systems through risk-mitigation activities.
contents.html_ja: DHS 国家サイバーセキュリティ部門の CSSP の目標は、連邦、州、地方、部族の各政府、ならびに産業用制御システムの所有者、運用者、ベンダーの間の取り組みを調整することにより、すべての重要インフラストラクチャおよび重要資源の分野の内部と分野間で、産業用制御システムのリスクを低減することです。CSSP は、リスク緩和活動を通じて、重要インフラストラクチャの制御システムに対するサイバー攻撃が成功する可能性と、その影響の深刻度を低減するための活動を調整しています。

contents.html: Critical infrastructures are dependent on information technology systems and computer networks for essential operations. Particular emphasis is placed on the reliability and resiliency of the systems that comprise and interconnect these infrastructures. NCSD collaborates with partners from across public, private, and international communities to advance this goal by developing and implementing coordinated security measures to protect against cyber threats.
contents.html_ja: 重要インフラストラクチャは、重要な運用を情報技術システムとコンピューターネットワークに依存しています。これらのインフラストラクチャを構成し相互接続するシステムの信頼性とレジリエンスには、特に重点が置かれています。NCSD は、サイバー脅威から守るための協調したセキュリティ対策を策定し実施することで、この目標を推進するため、官民および国際コミュニティのパートナーと協力しています。

contents.html: The Cyber Security Evaluation Tool (CSET<sup>™</sup>) is a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) product that assists organizations in protecting their key national cyber assets. It was developed under the direction of the DHS National Cyber Security Division (NCSD) by cybersecurity experts and with assistance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology. This tool provides users with a systematic and repeatable approach for assessing the security posture of their cyber systems and networks. It includes both high-level and detailed questions related to all industrial control and IT systems.
contents.html_ja: Cyber Security Evaluation Tool（CSET<sup>™</sup>）は、組織が国の重要なサイバー資産を保護するのを支援する、国土安全保障省（DHS）の製品です。DHS 国家サイバーセキュリティ部門（NCSD）の指揮のもと、サイバーセキュリティの専門家が、米国国立標準技術研究所の支援を受けて開発しました。このツールは、ユーザーに、自らのサイバーシステムとネットワークのセキュリティ態勢を評価するための、体系的で再現可能なアプローチを提供します。すべての産業用制御システムと IT システムに関する、高水準の質問と詳細な質問の両方が含まれています。

contents.html: CSET is a desktop software tool that guides users through a step-by-step process to assess their control system and information technology network security practices against recognized industry standards. The output from CSET is a prioritized list of recommendations for improving the cybersecurity posture of the organization's enterprise and industrial control cyber systems. The tool derives the recommendations from a database of cybersecurity standards, guidelines, and practices. Each recommendation is linked to a set of actions that can be applied to enhance cybersecurity controls.
contents.html_ja: CSET は、ユーザーが、制御システムと情報技術ネットワークのセキュリティ上の実践事項を、広く認められた業界標準に照らして評価する、段階的なプロセスをガイドする、デスクトップソフトウェアツールです。CSET の出力は、組織のエンタープライズと産業用制御サイバーシステムのサイバーセキュリティ態勢を改善するための推奨事項を、優先順位をつけて並べたリストです。このツールは、サイバーセキュリティの標準、ガイドライン、実践事項のデータベースから推奨事項を導き出します。各推奨事項は、サイバーセキュリティ管理策を強化するために適用できる一連のアクションに関連づけられています。

contents.html: CSET has been designed for easy installation and use on a stand-alone laptop or workstation. It incorporates a variety of available standards from organizations such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), International Organization for Standardization (ISO), U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), and others. When the tool user selects one or more of the standards, CSET will open a set of questions to be answered. The answers to these questions will be compared against a selected security assurance level, and a detailed report will be generated to show areas for potential improvement. CSET provides an excellent means to perform a self-assessment of the security posture of your control system environment.
contents.html_ja: CSET は、スタンドアロンのノートパソコンやワークステーションに簡単にインストールして使えるように設計されています。米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）、North American Electric Reliability Corporation（NERC）、国際標準化機構（ISO）、米国国防総省（DoD）などの組織が提供する、利用可能なさまざまな標準を取り込んでいます。ツールのユーザーが 1 つ以上の標準を選択すると、CSET は、回答すべき一連の質問を開きます。これらの質問への回答は、選択したセキュリティ保証レベルと比較され、改善の余地がある可能性のある領域を示す詳細な報告書が生成されます。CSET は、制御システム環境のセキュリティ態勢を自己評価するための優れた手段を提供します。

contents.html_ja: 15. 結論
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p275の章見出し

contents.html: The goals of the workshop were to look at recent (2 – 3 years) research results and deployment experiences that have occurred in cyber-physical areas across multiple industries. (e.g., healthcare, manufacturing, automotive, electric smart grid), and to determine if there are security requirements that are unique to CPS as opposed to strictly cyber or physical systems. Through these presentations on recent CPS cybersecurity research ideas and themes emerged. While some of these ideas are more critical from a security and safety technical standpoint, those that are policy and business oriented are equally crucial to implementing adequate security within CPS.
contents.html_ja: ワークショップの目標は、複数の産業（医療、製造、自動車、電力スマートグリッドなど）にわたってサイバーフィジカルの領域で得られた、最近（2～3 年）の研究成果と導入経験を検討すること、および、純粋なサイバーシステムや物理システムとは異なり、CPS に固有のセキュリティ要件があるかどうかを判断することでした。最近の CPS サイバーセキュリティ研究についてのこれらの発表を通じて、いくつかのアイデアとテーマが浮かび上がりました。これらのアイデアの一部は、セキュリティと安全性の技術的な観点からより重要ですが、政策やビジネスに関するものも、CPS 内で適切なセキュリティを実装するうえで同じように重要です。

contents.html: Attendees heard about the difficulty of detecting attacks on CPS. First, being able to tell the difference between an attack and a system failure can be difficult. Detecting an attack by analyzing massive amounts of data is both time consuming and difficult, as well as costly. In addition to attacks from outsiders, there are threats from inside sources. Finding malicious code inserted by an insider in over 100 million lines of code can be virtually impossible. All of these things make detecting cyber attacks challenging in CPS.
contents.html_ja: 参加者は、CPS に対する攻撃の検出が困難であることについて聞きました。第 1 に、攻撃とシステム障害の違いを見分けることが難しい場合があります。膨大な量のデータを分析して攻撃を検出することは、時間がかかり、困難であり、費用もかかります。部外者による攻撃に加えて、内部からの脅威もあります。1 億行を超えるコードの中から、内部者が挿入した悪意のあるコードを見つけることは、事実上不可能な場合があります。これらすべてが、CPS におけるサイバー攻撃の検出を困難にしています。

contents.html: Many presenters stressed the need for improved resiliency. While attacks to CPS will happen, a greater question is how will a system perform during and after an attack? Will the CPS continue to function at all? What will the consequences be? Without knowing the answers to these questions, building in layers of security and improving resiliency are critical to the continuing operations of CPS, especially when lives are dependent upon this continued operation. While a need for improved resiliency is not unique to CPS, the consequences of a system failure can be greater (potential loss of life) than in strictly cyber systems.
contents.html_ja: 多くの発表者が、レジリエンスの向上の必要性を強調しました。CPS への攻撃は起こるものですが、より大きな問題は、攻撃の最中と攻撃後にシステムがどのように動作するかです。CPS は機能し続けるのでしょうか。結果はどうなるのでしょうか。これらの問いへの答えが分からないまま、セキュリティの層を組み込み、レジリエンスを向上させることは、特に人命がその継続的な運用に依存している場合、CPS の運用継続にとって極めて重要です。レジリエンス向上の必要性は CPS に固有のものではありませんが、システム障害の結果は、純粋なサイバーシステムの場合よりも大きくなりえます（人命が失われる可能性）。

contents.html: Enabling robust cryptography in CPS remains a large challenge according to several presenters. The distribution, updating, and revocation of cryptographic keys presents a particular challenge as many CPS utilize hardware with certain constraints—such as amount of power, bandwidth, and processing capabilities—that cyber-only systems do not have.
contents.html_ja: 複数の発表者によると、CPS で堅牢な暗号技術を実現することは、依然として大きな課題です。暗号鍵の配布、更新、失効は、特に大きな課題です。多くの CPS が、電力、帯域幅、処理能力の量など、サイバーのみのシステムにはない一定の制約のあるハードウェアを利用しているためです。

contents.html: Likewise, usability needs to be more widely considered and improved in CPS. Without good usability, security measures may be bypassed or users may become inattentive to systems that may need immediate attention. While good usability is an important trait in cyber-only systems, it becomes critical to systems where poor usability can lead to inattention or accidental misuse in a system with physical impacts.
contents.html_ja: 同様に、CPS ではユーザビリティをより広く考慮し、改善する必要があります。優れたユーザビリティがないと、セキュリティ対策が回避されたり、ユーザーがすぐに対応が必要なシステムに対して注意を払わなくなったりする可能性があります。優れたユーザビリティは、サイバーのみのシステムでも重要な特性ですが、ユーザビリティが低いと、物理的な影響を持つシステムで、注意力の低下や偶発的な誤用につながりかねないため、そのようなシステムでは極めて重要になります。

contents.html: Virtual models are essential to the design and construction/assembly of reliable CPS, which are often so complex that testing of prototypes is either prohibitively expensive or impractical. Key characteristics of the models that are needed are robustness, with accurate representation of the full suite of properties of a CPS and the complicated environments in which they must operate, potential for use in verification and validation, and interoperability, allowing the combined use of multiple models or component modules. One of the unique impacts of not having usable, robust virtual models of CPS is that many systems rarely get patched as there is no acceptable way to foretell what the results of a patch may be to the system, and the possibility of the system being unavailable for some time has financial and safety/health risks that outweigh the risk of not patching.
contents.html_ja: 仮想モデルは、信頼性の高い CPS の設計と構築・組立に不可欠です。CPS はしばしば非常に複雑で、試作品の試験は、法外に費用がかかるか、実用的でないかのいずれかです。必要とされるモデルの主要な特性は、CPS の特性一式と、それが動作しなければならない複雑な環境を正確に表現する堅牢性、検証と妥当性確認に使用できる可能性、および複数のモデルやコンポーネントモジュールの併用を可能にする相互運用性です。使用可能で堅牢な CPS の仮想モデルがないことによる固有の影響の 1 つは、パッチがシステムにどのような結果をもたらすかを予測する許容可能な方法がなく、システムがしばらく利用できなくなる可能性に伴う財務上および安全・健康上のリスクが、パッチを適用しないリスクを上回るため、多くのシステムではパッチが適用されることがほとんどないことです。

contents.html: Failures of data integrity in CPS can result in tangible, real-world consequences not commonly seen in cyber-only systems. For example, in the military, loss of CPS data integrity can result in inaccurate or erroneous resource deployment, weapons targeting, etc. Likewise, a loss of integrity of data in networked medical devices can cause significant harm to a patient. The possible physical impacts present a significant, often unique challenge when designing cybersecurity for CPS.
contents.html_ja: CPS におけるデータの完全性の障害は、サイバーのみのシステムではあまり見られない、実世界での具体的な結果をもたらす可能性があります。たとえば、軍事では、CPS データの完全性が失われると、資源の配備や兵器の照準などが不正確または誤ったものになる可能性があります。同様に、ネットワーク接続された医療機器でデータの完全性が失われると、患者に重大な危害を及ぼす可能性があります。起こりうる物理的な影響は、CPS のサイバーセキュリティを設計する際に、重大で、しばしば固有の課題をもたらします。

contents.html: Finally, some of the most difficult challenges are those that are not only technical in nature, but include business and policy aspects. For instance, producing a persuasive business case for increased cybersecurity efforts can be difficult. Sometimes the likelihood of an incident can seem small so small that the cost of the appropriate countermeasures seem too expensive. This points to the need for research and development of both better measures for verifiable assurance in components and systems and also cyber-economic tools to help assess the costs associated with the range of potential cybersecurity incidents.
contents.html_ja: 最後に、最も困難な課題の一部は、技術的な性質のものだけでなく、ビジネスや政策の側面を含むものです。たとえば、サイバーセキュリティの取り組みを強化するための説得力のあるビジネスケースを作成することは、困難な場合があります。インシデントが起こる可能性が非常に小さいため、適切な対策の費用が高すぎると思えることがあります。これは、コンポーネントやシステムにおける検証可能な保証のためのより優れた手段と、さまざまな潜在的なサイバーセキュリティインシデントに伴うコストの評価に役立つサイバー経済学のツールの両方について、研究開発が必要であることを示しています。

contents.html: In addition to the unique cybersecurity requirements for most CPS for cryptography and modeling, there is also a requirement to keep systems available despite ongoing security incidents. For example, turning parts of the Smart Grid off in order to thwart an attack is not possible. In some CPS, there is a need to be able to detect small amounts of malicious code within a very large overall amount of code. In the semi-conductor example presented, there was a need to find 1,000 – 2,000 lines of malicious code in 1 to 2 million lines of code, and disposing of “suspect” semi-conductors would have had an enormous financial impact for the company.
contents.html_ja: ほとんどの CPS には、暗号技術とモデリングに関する固有のサイバーセキュリティ要件があるのに加えて、進行中のセキュリティインシデントがあってもシステムを利用可能に保つという要件もあります。たとえば、攻撃を阻止するためにスマートグリッドの一部を停止することはできません。一部の CPS では、非常に大量のコード全体の中から、少量の悪意のあるコードを検出できる必要があります。紹介された半導体の例では、100 万～200 万行のコードの中から、1,000～2,000 行の悪意のあるコードを見つける必要があり、「疑わしい」半導体を廃棄すれば、同社に莫大な財務上の影響が生じたことでしょう。

contents.html: There is also a need with CPS to consider potential impacts of cybersecurity incidents slightly differently. In every CPS, there is a physical action or reaction that is controlled by a cyber system. In many cases, there are many possible physical actions (e.g., modern airplanes have many physical actions/reactions controlled by cyber systems). This means that virtually every CPS has a health, safety, and environmental (HSE) impact. This makes potential impacts of cybersecurity incidents relatively high compared to traditional cyber-only systems. And since many of these systems have a high availability need, the choices for possible mitigations can be limited. These HSE impacts can also create a need for additional requirements often not needed for cyber-only systems, such as the requirement to coordinate with local emergency responders in case of incidents. HSE impacts need to be considered very carefully when identifying cybersecurity requirements for CPS.
contents.html_ja: CPS では、サイバーセキュリティインシデントの潜在的な影響を、少し違った形で考慮する必要もあります。あらゆる CPS には、サイバーシステムが制御する物理的な動作または反応があります。多くの場合、可能な物理的動作は数多くあります（たとえば、現代の飛行機には、サイバーシステムが制御する物理的な動作・反応が数多くあります）。これは、事実上すべての CPS が、健康、安全、環境（HSE）に影響を与えることを意味します。このため、サイバーセキュリティインシデントの潜在的な影響は、従来のサイバーのみのシステムと比べて比較的高くなります。また、これらのシステムの多くは可用性への要求が高いため、考えうる緩和策の選択肢が限られる場合があります。これらの HSE への影響により、インシデント発生時に地域の緊急対応要員と調整する要件など、サイバーのみのシステムでは必要とされないことが多い追加の要件が必要になる場合もあります。CPS のサイバーセキュリティ要件を特定する際には、HSE への影響を非常に慎重に考慮する必要があります。

1. Introduction

Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are hybrid networked cyber and engineered physical elements co-designed to create adaptive and predictive systems for enhanced performance.1, 2 These smart systems present a key opportunity to create a competitive advantage for U.S. industrial innova-tion and to improve the performance and reliability of new and existing systems. From smart manufacturing and the electric smart grid, to smart structures and transportation systems, CPS will pervasively impact the economy and society. Cybersecurity is a critical cross-cutting discipline that provides confidence that cyber-physical systems, their information, and supporting communications and information infrastructures are adequately safeguarded. CPS are increasingly being utilized in critical infrastructures and other settings. However, CPS have many unique characteristics, including the need for real-time response and extremely high availability, predictability, and reliability, which impacts cyber-security decisions. NIST is currently working in several CPS areas, including the electric smart grid, smart manufacturing, smart buildings, and networked automobiles. This work is being led by the Engineering Laboratory (EL), but also includes the Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML) and the Information Technology Laboratory (ITL). ITL has a number of key areas of expertise that are important to the evolution of CPS−interoperability, usability, reliability, and security. Since 2009, NIST has been very active in the area of the smart grid. ITL has been very active, providing leadership and expertise in a number of relevant areas, including communication networks, timing, and cybersecurity. ITL’s Computer Security Division (CSD) has provided leadership and expertise to the Smart Grid Interoperability Panel’s Cyber Security Working Group. Leveraging our broad expertise in relevant areas, we are now looking at the broader landscape of cyber-physical systems, and how cybersecurity fits into that landscape. CSD hosted a two-day workshop to explore CPS cybersecurity needs, with a focus on research results and real-world deployment experiences. On the first day, speakers addressed CPS across multiple sectors of industry (e.g., automotive, healthcare, semi-conductor manufacturing). The second day focused on cyber security needs of CPS in the electric smart grid. This document provides abstracts and corresponding slides from the plenary presentations at the workshop.3
1 For more information on this definition, please see George Arnold’s slides from the workshop.
2 Performance metrics include safety and security, reliability, agility and stability, efficiency and sustainability.

3 The website for the event is at http://www.nist.gov/itl/csd/cyberphysical-workshop.cfm, and the agenda is available at http://csrc.nist.gov/news_events/cps-workshop/cps-workshop-agenda_04-03-2012.pdf. The agenda document has links to electronic copies of the abstracts and slides.

Cyber Security Evaluation Tool

Critical infrastructures are dependent on information technology systems and computer networks for essential operations. Particular emphasis is placed on the reliability and resiliency of the sys-tems that comprise and interconnect these infrastructures. NCSD collaborates with partners from across public, private, and international communities to advance this goal by developing and im-plementing coordinated security measures to protect against cyber threats.

The Cyber Security Evaluation Tool (CSET™) is a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) product that assists organizations in protecting their key national cyber assets. It was developed under the direction of the DHS National Cyber Security Division (NCSD) by cybersecurity ex-perts and with assistance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology. This tool pro-vides users with a systematic and repeatable approach for assessing the security posture of their cyber systems and networks. It includes both high-level and detailed questions related to all in-dustrial control and IT systems.

CSET is a desktop software tool that guides users through a step-by-step process to assess their control system and information technology network security practices against recognized indus-try standards. The output from CSET is a prioritized list of recommendations for improving the cybersecurity posture of the organization's enterprise and industrial control cyber systems. The tool derives the recommendations from a database of cybersecurity standards, guidelines, and practices. Each recommendation is linked to a set of actions that can be applied to enhance cybersecurity controls.

CSET has been designed for easy installation and use on a stand-alone laptop or workstation. It incorporates a variety of available standards from organizations such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), International Organization for Standardization (ISO), U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), and others. When the tool user selects one or more of the standards, CSET will open a set of ques-tions to be answered. The answers to these questions will be compared against a selected security assurance level, and a detailed report will be generated to show areas for potential improvement. CSET provides an excellent means to perform a self-assessment of the security posture of your control system environment.

The goals of the workshop were to look at recent (2 – 3 years) research results and deployment experiences that have occurred in cyber-physical areas across multiple industries. (e.g., healthcare, manufacturing, automotive, electric smart grid), and to determine if there are security requirements that are unique to CPS as opposed to strictly cyber or physical systems. Through these presentations on recent CPS cybersecurity research ideas and themes emerged. While some of these ideas are more critical from a security and safety technical standpoint, those that are policy and business oriented are equally crucial to implementing adequate security within CPS.

Attendees heard about the difficulty of detecting attacks on CPS. First, being able to tell the dif-ference between an attack and a system failure can be difficult. Detecting an attack by analyzing massive amounts of data is both time consuming and difficult, as well as costly. In addition to attacks from outsiders, there are threats from inside sources. Finding malicious code inserted by an insider in over 100 million lines of code can be virtually impossible. All of these things make detecting cyber attacks challenging in CPS.

Many presenters stressed the need for improved resiliency. While attacks to CPS will happen, a greater question is how will a system perform during and after an attack? Will the CPS continue to function at all? What will the consequences be? Without knowing the answers to these ques-tions, building in layers of security and improving resiliency are critical to the continuing opera-tions of CPS, especially when lives are dependent upon this continued operation. While a need for improved resiliency is not unique to CPS, the consequences of a system failure can be greater (potential loss of life) than in strictly cyber systems.

Enabling robust cryptography in CPS remains a large challenge according to several presenters. The distribution, updating, and revocation of cryptographic keys presents a particular challenge as many CPS utilize hardware with certain constraints—such as amount of power, bandwidth, and processing capabilities—that cyber-only systems do not have.

Likewise, usability needs to be more widely considered and improved in CPS. Without good usability, security measures may be bypassed or users may become inattentive to systems that may need immediate attention. While good usability is an important trait in cyber-only systems, it becomes critical to systems where poor usability can lead to inattention or accidental misuse in a system with physical impacts.

Virtual models are essential to the design and construction/assembly of reliable CPS, which are often so complex that testing of prototypes is either prohibitively expensive or impractical. Key characteristics of the models that are needed are robustness, with accurate representation of the full suite of properties of a CPS and the complicated environments in which they must operate, potential for use in verification and validation, and interoperability, allowing the combined use of multiple models or component modules. One of the unique impacts of not having usable, ro-bust virtual models of CPS is that many systems rarely get patched as there is no acceptable way to foretell what the results of a patch may be to the system, and the possibility of the system be-ing unavailable for some time has financial and safety/health risks that outweigh the risk of not patching.

Failures of data integrity in CPS can result in tangible, real-world consequences not commonly seen in cyber-only systems. For example, in the military, loss of CPS data integrity can result in inaccurate or erroneous resource deployment, weapons targeting, etc. Likewise, a loss of integri-ty of data in networked medical devices can cause significant harm to a patient. The possible physical impacts present a significant, often unique challenge when designing cybersecurity for CPS.

Finally, some of the most difficult challenges are those that are not only technical in nature, but include business and policy aspects. For instance, producing a persuasive business case for in-creased cybersecurity efforts can be difficult. Sometimes the likelihood of an incident can seem small so small that the cost of the appropriate countermeasures seem too expensive. This points to the need for research and development of both better measures for verifiable assurance in components and systems and also cyber-economic tools to help assess the costs associated with the range of potential cybersecurity incidents.

In addition to the unique cybersecurity requirements for most CPS for cryptography and model-ing, there is also a requirement to keep systems available despite ongoing security incidents. For example, turning parts of the Smart Grid off in order to thwart an attack is not possible. In some CPS, there is a need to be able to detect small amounts of malicious code within a very large overall amount of code. In the semi-conductor example presented, there was a need to find 1,000 – 2,000 lines of malicious code in 1 to 2 million lines of code, and disposing of “suspect” semi-conductors would have had an enormous financial impact for the company.

There is also a need with CPS to consider potential impacts of cybersecurity incidents slightly differently. In every CPS, there is a physical action or reaction that is controlled by a cyber sys-tem. In many cases, there are many possible physical actions (e.g., modern airplanes have many physical actions/reactions controlled by cyber systems). This means that virtually every CPS has a health, safety, and environmental (HSE) impact. This makes potential impacts of cybersecurity incidents relatively high compared to traditional cyber-only systems. And since many of these systems have a high availability need, the choices for possible mitigations can be limited. These HSE impacts can also create a need for additional requirements often not needed for cyber-only systems, such as the requirement to coordinate with local emergency responders in case of inci-dents. HSE impacts need to be considered very carefully when identifying cybersecurity re-quirements for CPS.
The Computer Security Division plans to use the results of this workshop to inform future re-search, publications, and outreach activities in the area of CPS cybersecurity.
